title: tensordict.nn.dispatch does not have expected behavior
best_code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from tensordict import NonTensorData, TensorDict
from tensordict.nn import dispatch


def test(cls: type[nn.Module]) -> None:
    instance = cls()
    tensordict = TensorDict(
        {"a": torch.zeros(3, 5), "b": torch.ones(3, 2)}, batch_size=(3,)
    )

    print("Mode 1")
    print("legacy\n", instance(tensordict["a"], tensordict["b"]))
    print("up to date\n", instance(tensordict))

    print("Mode 2")
    instance.mode = "mode2"
    print("legacy\n", instance(tensordict["a"], tensordict["b"]))
    print("up to date\n", instance(tensordict))
error_description: The user is trying to use `dispatch` from `tensordict.nn` to make multimodal models retrocompatible with old scripts by mapping legacy inputs to different tensordict keys depending on the modality. The decorator approach fails because `self` cannot be accessed outside of methods. When attempting to call `dispatch` dynamically in the `forward` method wrapping `inner_forward`, it raises `TypeError: MyModule2.inner_forward() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given`.
repro_output: tensordict.nn.dispatch does not have expected behavior

trigger_conditions.other_conditions: Using tensordict.nn.dispatch decorator dynamically in forward method
